 Key points
 DA for central government employees goes from 60% to 63% of basic pay from 1 July 2026; pensioners' Dearness Relief rises the same way. 
 At Level 1 entry pay (₹18,000) DA rises by ₹540 a month; at Level 10 entry pay (₹56,100) by ₹1,683. 
 About 48.54 lakh employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners benefit; the cost is ₹10,016.10 crore a year. 
 State government, PSU and bank staff are not covered; their DA is set separately. 
 Advertisement
 New Delhi, 28 October: Dearness Allowance for central government employees will be 63% of basic pay from 1 July 2026, up from 60%. The Union Cabinet approved the 3% rise on 28 October. Pensioners get the same 3% rise in Dearness Relief.
 The Cabinet was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. About 48.54 lakh employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners will benefit, the government said in a release. The rise costs ₹10,016.10 crore a year for DA and DR together.
 The release said the rise is meant “to compensate against price rise”. It follows “the accepted formula, which is based on the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission”.
 Who gets what
 The new rate is 60% + 3% = 63% of basic pay or pension. Every ₹10,000 of basic pay adds ₹300 a month.
 Basic pay a month DA at 60% DA at 63% More each month 
 ₹18,000 (Level 1 entry) ₹10,800 ₹11,340 ₹540 
 ₹56,100 (Level 10 entry) ₹33,660 ₹35,343 ₹1,683 
 The higher DA counts from 1 July 2026. So the extra amount for each month since July is due as arrears — ₹540 a month at Level 1 entry pay. The release does not say when the Department of Expenditure will issue its order, which pay offices act on, or when the arrears will be paid. The DA arrear calculator works out your own arrears.
 What does not change
 This decision does not cover state government employees and pensioners, PSU staff on industrial DA, or bank employees. Their DA is set separately — by their state government, the Department of Public Enterprises or the Indian Banks’ Association.
 How DA has moved
 Effective from DA rate 
 July 2022 38% 
 January 2023 42% 
 July 2023 46% 
 January 2024 50% 
 July 2024 53% 
 January 2025 55% 
 July 2025 58% 
 January 2026 60% 
 July 2026 63% (60% + the 3% approved) 
 In the last two rounds, the Department of Expenditure’s order came a few days after the Cabinet. The July 2025 rise to 58% was approved on 1 October 2025 and ordered on 6 October 2025. The January 2026 rise to 60% was approved on 18 April 2026 and ordered on 22 April 2026. Use the DA calculator to work out the new amount on your own basic pay or pension.
 Source: PIB — Cabinet, “Cabinet approves Dearness Allowance to Central Government employees and Dearness Relief to Pensioners”, Release ID 2329484, 28 October 2026.

 Critical AdSense behaviour: adsbygoogle.push({}) does NOT bind to
 a specific . It says "process the next unbound in DOM
 order." So if you push N times, AdSense binds the first N 
 slots it finds.
 Live investigation (2026-05-29) showed the right sidebar still
 loading late on indianpaycalculator.in. DOM order of :
 1. LEFT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-left)
 2-5. Display banners (4× AdBanner inside page content)
 6. RIGHT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-right, after main slot)
 7. Mobile anchor (StickyAnchorAd at body end)
 Previously this script pushed twice (one per sidebar). Those 2
 pushes bound LEFT + Display#1, NOT LEFT + RIGHT. The other 5
 slots only got bound as AdBanner.client:visible islands hydrated
 on scroll — meaning the right sidebar was bound 6th, after the
 user scrolled past every in-page banner. That's the "right side
 opens very late" complaint.
 Fix: push once per SSR'd ad slot. AdSense binds them all in DOM
 order at body parse end — no React hydration wait, no scroll-to-
 view wait. Subsequent React useEffect pushes (from AdUnit /
 StickyAnchorAd) become no-ops since the AdUnit effect skips when
 data-adsbygoogle-status is already set. --> component was removed 2026-05-29 to eliminate the
